payload.title: Publication visual style profiles for shared image generation
payload.description:
Build publication-specific visual direction into the shared image curation and generation workflow (PPY-0111742e), so editor UI, CLI, MCP and agents use the same publication-owned source of truth, analogous to mission and policies. This is planning only; preserve the current illustration rules and ownership decisions. User asks for Gemini and OpenAI support and for one image or sets of four; do not imply a particular paid model or price has been approved.

Visual direction: provide an editor-managed, versioned publication profile with human-readable creative guidance plus structured fields, including visual identity and palette/tokens, preferred/avoided techniques, subject and representation guidance, formats, safe zones, example images and negative examples, attribution and disclosure guidance. Separate brand identity from image treatments (for example editorial illustration, photo, abstract, diagram) and asset uses (cover, inline, social), with site defaults and optional section/Story overrides. Specify precedence, missing-profile behavior, version snapshots, and how backend doctrine relates to site-repository design artifacts so they do not silently diverge. Machines on Machines already has a design system and figure rules; do not force all publications into its style. Only an explicit publisher choice adopts generated-image treatment that conflicts with existing rules. Reference imagery should control visual treatment rather than insert pictured people, logos or compositions.

Inspiration: https://github.com/belchman/nano-banana-aware composes a master style prompt, per-asset templates, negatives and optional visual references, maintains generation history, and offers guided and automatic flows. Adapt these concepts as shared provider-neutral operations rather than relying on a Claude-only skill, CLI installation, magenta chromakey or unverified prompt compliance. Consider deterministic overlays for exact text, and post-processing only when a selected use needs it.

Generation and review: shared image service resolves the style profile, brief, asset purpose and provider capabilities, supports one candidate or four separately selectable candidates, enables either variations within one treatment or intentionally different suitable treatments, and returns each candidate progressively with partial failures and retries. Every candidate has an id, usable preview, accessibility draft, provider and actual model, generation timestamp, style profile version, reference assets and effective prompt/settings. Preserve author/selection provenance and distinguish agent draft selection from human approval. Store candidates privately until applied; reuse existing MediaAsset application and projection path. Users can inspect, iterate, accept a candidate, or keep the placeholder. UI waves of four, CLI JSON and authenticated MCP tools must operate on the same records and authorization logic.

Provider adapters: support configurable Gemini and OpenAI interfaces behind a single capability contract, with per-model support for reference images, aspect ratio, output count and native transparency checked at runtime. Four candidates may require four jobs; do not request a single four-panel collage or assume every provider honors an output count. Expose prompt/style references sent to the provider and do not silently change the provider. Specify what can be guaranteed (dimensions, metadata, known palette checks where applicable) versus creative guidance requiring human/agent evaluation. Log partial results, errors and retries and test tenant isolation and no image published by selection alone.

Acceptance scenarios:
- Given two publications with distinct visual profiles, generation through UI, CLI or MCP resolves and snapshots the correct publication profile and never leaks the other publication's guidance or references.
- Given a publication default, asset type, section and Story override, the effective style and its precedence are previewable before generating and recorded on the candidate.
- Given a request for one or four options, return separate candidate records; surface individual failures and permit retry without discarding successful candidates.
- Given a user or an authorized agent selects a candidate, preserve the identity and actual provenance; only an explicit apply action updates the intended Story or Reference, and no human approval is fabricated.
- Given a provider cannot support a requested option, return a clear capability error or a user-visible agreed fallback without silently changing the model.
- Given a profile change, existing generated assets retain the original profile/version while later requests use the updated one; repeatability is best-effort rather than promised exact reproduction.
